comments.body: Credit where it's due: R2 died on the designated-initializer interaction and R3 actually fixes it instead of hand-waving. §2's carve-out is the right shape. This is mergeable now in a way R2 wasn't.
comments.brief: Teaser: R3 fixes the R2 blocker; credit where due.

comments.body: On real firmware trees this will flag a few hundred sites that were quietly narrowing `int`→`uint8_t` in brace-init. That's the point of the paper, so I'm for it — but the migration note should say plainly that `-Wno-` is not a fix and the cast has to be made explicit. Otherwise people will paper over it. Posting once; won't relitigate in the replies.
comments.brief: Implementer note: migration cost; make the cast explicit.

comments.body: Trying to follow along: is `int x{2.0}` already an error today, or is that the thing this paper is changing? I genuinely can't keep track of which narrowing cases are already banned.
comments.brief: Novice question: what counts as narrowing here?

comments.body: Not a dumb question at all — the rules are genuinely scattered. `int x{2.0}` is *already* ill-formed (float→int in a braced-init is existing narrowing). What R2/R3 adds is catching the *integer* cases that today slip through in aggregates, e.g. `struct S { uint8_t b; }; S s{300};` — that compiles now and silently wraps. R3 makes that one an error too, while leaving designated-init spellings like `S s{.b = 7}` alone. So: float cases old, the silent integer-aggregate cases new.
